records.literal_gloss: And sent Yahweh Nathan to David, and he came to him and said to him, two men were in city one, one rich and one poor.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent Nathan to David. And he came to him and said to him, "There were two men in one city, one rich and the other poor.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent Nathan to David. He came to him and said, "In a certain city there were two men, one of them rich and the other poor.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} sent Nathan to David. Nathan came to him and said, "Two men lived in a town. One was rich, and the other was poor.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} envoya Nathan à David. Et il vint vers lui et lui dit : « Il y avait deux hommes dans une ville, l’un riche et l’autre pauvre.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} envoya Nathan auprès de David. Nathan vint le trouver et lui dit : « Dans une ville, il y avait deux hommes ; l’un était riche, l’autre pauvre.

am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ናታንን ወደ ዳዊት ላከው። ናታንም ወደ እርሱ መጥቶ እንዲህ አለው፦ «በአንድ ከተማ ሁለት ሰዎች ይኖሩ ነበር። አንዱ ሀብታም ነበረ፤ ሌላው ደግሞ ድሀ ነበረ።

ru.L: И послал {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Нафана к Давиду. И пришёл он к нему и сказал ему: «Два человека были в одном городе, один богатый, а другой бедный.
ru.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} послал Нафана к Давиду. Нафан пришёл к нему и сказал: «В одном городе жили два человека: один богатый, а другой бедный.
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} послал Нафана к Давиду. Нафан пришёл к нему и сказал: «В одном городе жили два человека. Один был богатый, а другой бедный.

uk.L: І послав {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} Натана до Давида. І прийшов він до нього, і сказав йому: «Двоє чоловіків були в одному місті, один багатий, а другий бідний.
uk.B: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} послав Натана до Давида. Він прийшов до нього й сказав: «В одному місті жили двоє чоловіків, один багатий, а другий бідний.
uk.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}} послав Натана до Давида. Натан прийшов до нього й сказав: «У місті жили двоє чоловіків. Один був багатий, а другий бідний.

decisions.choice: the LORD sent Nathan: God answers what David did in chapter 11
decisions.reason: The last words of chapter 11 were that what David had done was evil in Yahweh's eyes (11:27). Now Yahweh acts. Nathan is the prophet who brought David the promise of a lasting house (7:2-17); he now brings God's judgment.

decisions.choice: two men: a story told as a case for the king to judge
decisions.reason: Nathan does not say at first that this is a parable. He tells it like a real complaint brought to the king, who was the highest judge in the land (15:2-4). David is meant to give his verdict before he sees that the case is about himself. A wise woman uses the same method in 14:4-11, and a prophet in 1 Kings 20:39-41.

decisions.choice: poor: a man with little or nothing
decisions.reason: The word describes someone without property or means (Proverbs 13:23; 1 Samuel 18:23, where David calls himself "a poor man"). It sets up the contrast with the rich man's many flocks.

decisions.choice: Nathan came to him
decisions.reason: Readable names Nathan, where the Hebrew says only "he", so that the reader does not take the subject to be David.

decisions.choice: Nathan's story in the imperfect and the passé composé at every level ("il y avait", "il a pris")
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The parable is speech to the king, told as a case for him to judge (m2), so it takes the tenses of spoken French at every level, as the style guide sets for stories told inside speech. The quotation stays open to the end of verse 4.

decisions.choice: "Natán"
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note and the published Psalm 51 title. The parable is drafted from the Hebrew gloss, as the Samuel terms note asks for this chapter.

decisions.choice: Nathan tells the story to "vua" as a case to be judged, without any address in it
decisions.reason: Nathan calls David "vua" as the Samuel terms note sets; the story itself is told plainly, as a case brought before the king (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: Nathan tells his story to the king in the formal polite style (합쇼체), as a case brought for judgment
alternatives: the plain narrative style inside the story
decisions.reason: A subject presenting a case to the king speaks 합쇼체 throughout; the story's own events are told with -었습니다.

decisions.choice: Natã
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the prophet is "Natã", the usual Brazilian form, with the nasal ending of "Miriã" and "Midiã", as in chapter 7 and Luke 3:31 in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in this chapter's Amharic (verses 9-10, 14, 25)
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic.

decisions.choice: "भेजा", as in chapter 11
decisions.reason: The sending of chapter 11 is answered: now Yahweh sends (m1). Hindi keeps the same verb "भेजना".

decisions.choice: "धनी ... कंगाल" (Literal, Balanced); "अमीर ... ग़रीब" (Readable)
decisions.reason: "कंगाल" says a man with nothing (m3); Readable has the everyday pair.

decisions.choice: Nathan's story told plainly, in the third person; Nathan says "आप" to the king (verse 7)
decisions.reason: The parable is told as a case for the king to judge (m2), so the story itself has no address; when Nathan turns to David he keeps "आप", the courtier's address of chapter 7.

decisions.choice: "богатый ... бедный"
decisions.reason: The story is told as a case for the king to judge (meaning m2); Russian keeps the plain pair "богатый" and "бедный" at every level, with "богач" and "бедняк" in verse 4 where the story moves on.

decisions.choice: Nathan tells the case to the king in です・ます; God's words inside his speech (12:7-12) are plain
decisions.reason: As 7:3: Nathan speaks to the king with respect, as a case brought for judgment (m2).

en.L: The rich [man] had very many flocks and herds.
en.B: The rich man had a great many sheep and cattle.
en.R: The rich man had very large flocks of sheep and herds of cattle.

es.B: El hombre rico tenía muchísimas ovejas y reses.
es.R: El hombre rico tenía rebaños muy grandes de ovejas y manadas de ganado.

fr.L: Le riche avait du petit et du gros bétail en très grand nombre.
fr.B: Le riche avait des moutons et des bœufs en très grand nombre.
fr.R: L’homme riche avait de très grands troupeaux de moutons et de bœufs.

ja.R: お金持ちは、とてもたくさんの羊の群れと牛の群れを持っていました。

decisions.choice: flocks and herds: sheep and goats, and cattle
decisions.reason: The first word covers small livestock, sheep and goats together; the second covers cattle. Together they sum up a herdsman's wealth (Genesis 13:5; 1 Samuel 27:9).

decisions.choice: sheep and cattle (Balanced); flocks of sheep and herds of cattle (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the animals, since "flocks and herds" is less familiar. Readable keeps "flocks" and "herds" and says what they were made up of.

source.text: וְלָרָ֣שׁ אֵֽין־כֹּ֗ל כִּי֩ אִם־כִּבְשָׂ֨ה אַחַ֤ת קְטַנָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָנָ֔ה וַיְחַיֶּ֕הָ וַתִּגְדַּ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ וְעִם־בָּנָ֖יו יַחְדָּ֑ו מִפִּתּ֨וֹ תֹאכַ֜ל וּמִכֹּס֤וֹ תִשְׁתֶּה֙ וּבְחֵיק֣וֹ תִשְׁכָּ֔ב וַתְּהִי־ל֖וֹ כְּבַֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And to the poor [man] there was not anything except ewe-lamb one small which he had bought, and he kept her alive, and she grew up with him and with his sons together; from his morsel she would eat, and from his cup she would drink, and in his bosom she would lie, and she was to him like a daughter.

en.L: But the poor [man] had nothing except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought. And he kept it alive, and it grew up with him and with his {{gender:children|sons}} together. It would eat from his morsel and drink from his cup and lie in his bosom, and it was like a daughter to him.
en.B: But the poor man had nothing except one little ewe lamb that he had bought. He nurtured it, and it grew up with him alongside his {{gender:children|sons}}. It shared his bit of bread, drank from his cup and lay in his arms; it was like a daughter to him.
en.R: But the poor man had nothing except one little female lamb that he had bought. He took care of it, and it grew up in his home together with his {{gender:children|sons}}. It ate from his plate and drank from his cup, and it even slept in his arms. The lamb was like a daughter to him.

es.L: Pero el pobre no tenía nada sino una sola corderita pequeña que había comprado. Y la crió, y ella creció con él y con sus hijos juntamente. De su bocado comía, y de su copa bebía, y en su regazo dormía, y era para él como una hija.
es.B: Pero el pobre no tenía más que una corderita que había comprado. Él la cuidó, y la corderita creció con él y junto con sus hijos. Comía de su pedazo de pan, bebía de su copa y dormía en sus brazos; era para él como una hija.
es.R: Pero el hombre pobre no tenía nada más que una corderita que había comprado. Él la cuidaba, y ella creció en su casa junto con sus hijos. Comía de su plato y bebía de su vaso, y hasta dormía en sus brazos. La corderita era como una hija para él.

fr.L: Mais le pauvre n’avait rien, sinon une seule petite brebis qu’il avait achetée. Et il la nourrissait, et elle grandissait avec lui et avec ses {{gender:enfants|fils}} ensemble. Elle mangeait de sa bouchée, et buvait de sa coupe, et couchait sur son sein, et elle était pour lui comme une fille.
fr.B: Mais le pauvre n’avait rien d’autre qu’une petite brebis qu’il avait achetée. Il l’élevait, et elle grandissait chez lui avec ses {{gender:enfants|fils}}. Elle partageait son morceau de pain, buvait dans sa coupe et dormait dans ses bras ; elle était pour lui comme une fille.
fr.R: Mais l’homme pauvre n’avait rien, à part une petite agnelle qu’il avait achetée. Il s’en occupait, et elle grandissait dans sa maison avec ses {{gender:enfants|fils}}. Elle mangeait dans son assiette et buvait dans sa coupe, et elle dormait même dans ses bras. Cette agnelle était pour lui comme une fille.

sw.L: Lakini maskini hakuwa na kitu chochote isipokuwa mwana-kondoo mmoja mdogo wa kike aliyekuwa amemnunua. Akamlea, naye akakua pamoja naye na pamoja na watoto wake. Alikula katika tonge lake na kunywa katika kikombe chake na kulala kifuani mwake, naye alikuwa kwake kama binti.
sw.B: Lakini yule maskini hakuwa na chochote isipokuwa mwana-kondoo mmoja mdogo wa kike aliyekuwa amemnunua. Alimtunza, naye akakua pamoja naye na watoto wake. Alishiriki kipande chake cha mkate, akanywa katika kikombe chake na kulala mikononi mwake; alikuwa kwake kama binti.
sw.R: Lakini yule maskini hakuwa na chochote isipokuwa mwana-kondoo mmoja mdogo wa kike aliyekuwa amemnunua. Alimtunza, naye akakua nyumbani mwake pamoja na watoto wake. Alikula katika sahani yake na kunywa katika kikombe chake, hata alilala mikononi mwake. Mwana-kondoo huyo alikuwa kama binti kwake.

vi.L: Còn người nghèo chẳng có gì ngoài một con chiên cái nhỏ mà ông đã mua. Ông nuôi nó, và nó lớn lên cùng với ông và các con ông. Nó ăn miếng ăn của ông, uống chén của ông, nằm trong lòng ông, và nó như một đứa con gái đối với ông.
vi.B: Còn người nghèo chẳng có gì ngoài một con chiên cái nhỏ ông đã mua về. Ông nuôi nấng nó, và nó lớn lên trong nhà cùng với các con ông. Nó ăn chung miếng bánh của ông, uống chung chén của ông, và nằm trong vòng tay ông; nó như con gái của ông vậy.
vi.R: Còn người nghèo chẳng có gì ngoài một con chiên cái nhỏ ông đã mua. Ông chăm sóc nó, và nó lớn lên trong nhà cùng với các con của ông. Nó ăn chung đĩa và uống chung chén với ông, có khi còn ngủ trong vòng tay ông. Con chiên ấy như đứa con gái của ông.

ko.L: 그러나 가난한 [사람에게는] 그가 사서 키운 작은 암양 새끼 한 마리 말고는 아무것도 없었습니다. 그리고 그 [양은] 그와 그의 자식들과 함께 자랐습니다. 그것은 그의 음식 조각을 먹고, 그의 잔으로 마시고, 그의 품에 누웠으며, 그에게 딸과 같았습니다.
ko.B: 그러나 가난한 사람에게는 사다가 기른 작은 암양 새끼 한 마리밖에 없었습니다. 그 양은 그의 집에서 그의 자식들과 함께 자랐습니다. 그 양은 그가 먹는 빵 조각을 나누어 먹고, 그의 잔으로 마시고, 그의 품에 안겨 잤습니다. 그에게 그 양은 딸과 같았습니다.
ko.R: 그러나 가난한 사람에게는 사 온 작은 암양 새끼 한 마리밖에 없었습니다. 그는 그 양을 돌보았고, 양은 그의 집에서 아이들과 함께 자랐습니다. 양은 그의 그릇에 담긴 것을 같이 먹고 그의 잔으로 같이 마셨습니다. 밤에는 그의 품에 안겨 잤습니다. 그 양은 그에게 딸과 같았습니다.

pt.L: Mas o pobre não tinha nada, a não ser uma só cordeirinha que tinha comprado. E ele a manteve viva, e ela cresceu com ele e com os seus filhos; do seu bocado ela comia, e do seu copo bebia, e no seu colo se deitava, e ela era para ele como uma filha.
pt.B: Mas o pobre não tinha nada, a não ser uma cordeirinha que ele tinha comprado. Ele a criou, e ela cresceu com ele e com os seus filhos. Ela comia do seu pedaço de pão, bebia do seu copo e dormia nos seus braços; era como uma filha para ele.
pt.R: Mas o pobre não tinha nada, a não ser uma cordeirinha que tinha comprado. Ele cuidou dela, e ela cresceu na casa dele, junto com os filhos dele. Ela comia do prato dele, bebia do copo dele e até dormia no colo dele. A cordeirinha era como uma filha para ele.

am.L: ለድሀው ግን ከገዛት ከአንዲት ትንሽ የበግ ጠቦት በቀር ምንም አልነበረውም፤ አሳደጋትም፤ ከእርሱና ከልጆቹ ጋር በአንድነት አደገች፤ ከቁራሹ ትበላ፣ ከጽዋውም ትጠጣ፣ በብብቱም ትተኛ ነበር፤ ለእርሱም እንደ ሴት ልጅ ነበረች።
am.B: ድሀው ሰው ግን ከገዛት ከአንዲት ትንሽ እንስት ጠቦት በቀር ምንም አልነበረውም። ተንከባከባት፤ እርሷም ከእርሱና ከልጆቹ ጋር አብራ አደገች። ከቁራሽ እንጀራው ትካፈል፣ ከጽዋው ትጠጣ፣ በእቅፉም ትተኛ ነበር፤ ለእርሱም እንደ ሴት ልጅ ነበረች።
am.R: ድሀው ሰው ግን ከገዛት ከአንዲት ትንሽ እንስት ጠቦት በቀር ምንም አልነበረውም። ይንከባከባት ነበር፤ እርሷም በቤቱ ከልጆቹ ጋር አብራ አደገች። ከሳህኑ ትበላ፣ ከጽዋው ትጠጣ ነበር፤ በእቅፉም እንኳ ትተኛ ነበር። ጠቦቲቱ ለእርሱ እንደ ሴት ልጅ ነበረች።

hi.L: पर कंगाल के पास भेड़ की एक छोटी बच्ची को छोड़ कुछ भी न था, जिसे उसने मोल लिया था। और उसने उसे पाला, और वह उसके और उसके {{gender:बच्चों|बेटों}} के साथ बड़ी हुई। वह उसके कौर में से खाती, और उसके प्याले में से पीती, और उसकी गोद में सोती थी, और वह उसके लिए बेटी के समान थी।
hi.B: पर कंगाल के पास भेड़ की एक छोटी बच्ची को छोड़ और कुछ न था, जिसे उसने मोल लिया था। उसने उसे पाला-पोसा, और वह उसके {{gender:बच्चों|बेटों}} के साथ उसी के घर में बड़ी हुई। वह उसकी रोटी में से खाती, उसके प्याले में से पीती, और उसकी बाँहों में सोती थी। वह उसके लिए बेटी के समान थी।
hi.R: पर ग़रीब आदमी के पास भेड़ की एक छोटी बच्ची के सिवा कुछ नहीं था, जिसे उसने ख़रीदा था। उसने उसकी देखभाल की, और वह उसके घर में उसके {{gender:बच्चों|बेटों}} के साथ बड़ी हुई। वह उसकी थाली में से खाती और उसके प्याले में से पीती थी, और उसकी बाँहों में सो भी जाती थी। वह मेमनी उसके लिए बेटी जैसी थी।

ru.L: А у бедного не было ничего, кроме одной маленькой овечки, которую он купил. И он выкормил её, и она выросла у него вместе с его {{gender:детьми|сыновьями}}; от его куска она ела, и из его чаши пила, и на его груди спала, и была ему как дочь.
ru.B: А у бедного не было ничего, кроме одной маленькой овечки, которую он купил. Он выходил её, и она росла у него вместе с его {{gender:детьми|сыновьями}}. Она делила с ним его кусок хлеба, пила из его чаши и спала у него на руках; она была ему как дочь.
ru.R: А у бедного не было ничего, кроме одной маленькой овечки, которую он купил. Он заботился о ней, и она росла в его доме вместе с его {{gender:детьми|сыновьями}}. Она ела из его тарелки, пила из его чашки и даже спала у него на руках. Овечка была ему как дочь.

ja.L: しかし、貧しい[男]には、自分が買ってきた一匹の小さな雌の小羊のほかには、何もありませんでした。彼はそれを養い、それは彼と彼の子どもたちと共に育ちました。彼のパンの一切れから食べ、彼の杯から飲み、彼のふところで眠り、彼にとって娘のようでした。
ja.B: しかし、貧しい人には、自分で買ってきた一匹の小さな雌の小羊しかありませんでした。彼はその小羊を大切に育て、小羊は彼の子どもたちと一緒に大きくなりました。小羊は彼のわずかなパンを分けてもらい、彼の杯から飲み、彼の腕に抱かれて眠りました。彼にとって、娘のような存在だったのです。
ja.R: しかし、貧しい人は、自分で買った一匹の小さな雌の小羊のほかには、何も持っていませんでした。彼はその小羊をかわいがって世話をしました。小羊は、彼の家で子どもたちと一緒に大きくなりました。彼の皿から食べ、彼のコップから飲み、彼の腕の中で眠りさえしました。その小羊は、彼にとって娘のようでした。

uk.L: А в бідного не було нічого, крім однієї маленької овечки, яку він купив. І він годував її, і вона росла з ним і з його {{gender:дітьми|синами}} разом. З його шматка вона їла, і з його чаші пила, і на його лоні лежала, і була йому, як дочка.
uk.B: А в бідного не було нічого, крім однієї маленької овечки, яку він купив. Він доглядав її, і вона росла в нього разом з його {{gender:дітьми|синами}}. Вона їла з його шматка хліба, пила з його чаші й спала в його обіймах. Вона була йому, як дочка.
uk.R: А в бідного не було нічого, крім однієї маленької овечки, яку він купив. Він доглядав її, і вона росла в його домі разом з його {{gender:дітьми|синами}}. Вона їла з його тарілки й пила з його чаші, і навіть спала в його обіймах. Овечка була йому, як дочка.

decisions.choice: one little ewe lamb: a single animal kept as part of the family
decisions.reason: A poor household might own one lamb and raise it by hand. This one is treated like a child of the house: it eats the man's own food and sleeps in his arms. Its loss is the loss of something loved, not only of property.

decisions.choice: would eat, would drink, would lie: what happened day after day
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe the lamb's daily life with the family, not a single meal.

decisions.choice: lay in his bosom ... like a daughter: words that point toward the real case
decisions.reason: "Bosom" is the word for a close embrace, used of a wife in verse 8 and in Deuteronomy 13:7; 28:54. The lamb is "like a daughter" (Hebrew *bat*), and the woman in chapter 11 is Bathsheba, whose name begins with the same word. The story is told so that David can hear it as being about a man's beloved, though he does not yet see it.

decisions.choice: his sons: his children
decisions.reason: The plural of "son" often covers a man's children of both sexes. Nothing in the story limits it to boys.

decisions.choice: shared his bit of bread, lay in his arms (Balanced); ate from his plate, slept in his arms (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Morsel" is a piece of bread, a share of the man's own meal; Readable says "ate from his plate". "Bosom" becomes "arms". Readable adds "even" to show that this is the most striking detail.

decisions.choice: ses {{gender:enfants|fils}}
decisions.reason: The plural covers a man's children of both sexes (m4), so French takes the inclusive "enfants" by default, as the English does; "brebis" and "agnelle" keep the female animal, which the story uses to point toward Bathsheba.

decisions.choice: "sus hijos", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters, so the English gender span on "children" / "sons" has no Spanish counterpart, as the Pentateuch note sets.

decisions.choice: watoto wake
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on "children|sons". "Watoto" (children) is the natural Swahili word for a man's family at home; the traditional "wana" would not narrow the meaning, so there is no span.

decisions.choice: "các con" with no gender setting
alternatives: "các con trai" as a second wording
decisions.reason: His sons are his children (meaning decision); Vietnamese "các con" includes both, so the English gender setting has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: "자식들" (L) and "아이들" (R) with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: The Korean words already mean children of both sexes.

decisions.choice: a cordeirinha
decisions.reason: The diminutive "cordeirinha" says in one word that the lamb was small and female (m1) and carries the tenderness of a pet raised by hand, which is the point of the story; Literal adds "uma só" for "one".

decisions.choice: os seus filhos, without a gender setting
decisions.reason: Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters (m4), as in the Pentateuch and 1 Samuel in Portuguese, so there is no second wording for the English gender setting to choose.

decisions.choice: "his sons" is "ልጆቹ" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Amharic "ልጆች" already means children of either sex, so the two options of the English setting have one Amharic wording; "ወንዶች ልጆቹ" would narrow what the Hebrew plural here includes.

decisions.choice: the ewe lamb is "ጠቦት" (feminine: "ትንሽ ጠቦት", "እርሷ"); Readable keeps her as "she"
decisions.reason: "ጠቦት" is the young lamb of the Pentateuch's Amharic; the feminine forms keep the picture of a daughter that the parable builds toward.

decisions.choice: ewe lamb: "भेड़ की एक छोटी बच्ची" (every level), "मेमनी" (Readable, after the first mention)
decisions.reason: A female lamb (m1); Hindi "बच्ची" keeps the feminine, which matters for "like a daughter" and the picture of Bathsheba behind it (m3).

decisions.choice: "{{gender:बच्चों|बेटों}}"
decisions.reason: "His sons" means his children (m4); Hindi has the same two choices the English setting offers.

decisions.choice: "उसकी गोद में" (Literal); "उसकी बाँहों में" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Bosom" is kept at Literal as Hindi "गोद" (lap, bosom); the same word comes back in verse 8 ("your master's wives into your bosom").

decisions.choice: "{{gender:детьми|сыновьями}}"
decisions.reason: His "sons" are his children (meaning m4); the default "дети" includes daughters, with the traditional "сыновья" as the alternative, as the English span does.

decisions.choice: "на его груди спала" (Literal); "спала у него на руках" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "in his bosom" points toward the real case, a wife (meaning m3); Literal keeps the picture, the other levels say it as Russian would of a pet, as the English "in his arms" does.

decisions.choice: imperfective "ела", "пила", "спала"
decisions.reason: What happened day after day (meaning m2); Russian says it with the imperfective.

decisions.choice: banav "子どもたち" with no gender span where the English has children|sons
decisions.reason: Japanese 子どもたち is already inclusive (m4).

decisions.choice: kivsah "雌の小羊" at every level
decisions.reason: As GEN-consistency 小羊; the female lamb is the point of the story (m1).

source.text: וַיָּ֣בֹא הֵלֶךְ֮ לְאִ֣ישׁ הֶֽעָשִׁיר֒ וַיַּחְמֹ֗ל לָקַ֤חַת מִצֹּאנוֹ֙ וּמִבְּקָר֔וֹ לַעֲשׂ֕וֹת לָאֹרֵ֖חַ הַבָּא־ל֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֗ח אֶת־כִּבְשַׂת֙ הָאִ֣ישׁ הָרָ֔אשׁ וַֽיַּעֲשֶׂ֔הָ לָאִ֖ישׁ הַבָּ֥א אֵלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And came a traveler to [the] man the rich, and he spared to take from his flock and from his herd to prepare for the wayfarer who had come to him; and he took [the] ewe-lamb of the man the poor and prepared it for the man who had come to him.

en.L: And a traveler came to the rich man, and he spared taking from his own flock and from his own herd to prepare for the wayfarer who had come to him. And he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him."
en.B: Then a traveler came to the rich man. He did not want to take one of his own sheep or cattle to prepare for the visitor who had come to him. So he took the poor man's ewe lamb and prepared it for his guest."
en.R: One day a traveler came to visit the rich man. The rich man did not want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle to make a meal for his guest. So he took the poor man's lamb and cooked it for the visitor."

es.L: Y vino un viajero al hombre rico, y él se privó de tomar de sus ovejas y de sus vacas para preparar[le] al caminante que había venido a él. Y tomó la corderita del hombre pobre y la preparó para el hombre que había venido a él».
es.B: Entonces llegó un viajero a casa del hombre rico. Él no quiso tomar una de sus propias ovejas o reses para preparársela al visitante que había llegado. Así que tomó la corderita del pobre y se la preparó a su huésped».
es.R: Un día llegó un viajero a visitar al hombre rico. El rico no quiso matar ninguna de sus propias ovejas ni de sus reses para hacerle una comida a su invitado. Así que tomó la corderita del hombre pobre y la cocinó para el visitante».

fr.L: Et un voyageur est venu chez l’homme riche, et il a épargné de prendre de son petit bétail et de son gros bétail pour apprêter [un repas] au passant qui était venu chez lui. Et il a pris la brebis de l’homme pauvre et l’a apprêtée pour l’homme qui était venu chez lui. »
fr.B: Un jour, un voyageur est arrivé chez le riche. Celui-ci n’a pas voulu prendre une de ses propres bêtes, mouton ou bœuf, pour la préparer au visiteur venu chez lui. Il a donc pris la brebis du pauvre et l’a préparée pour son hôte. »
fr.R: Un jour, un voyageur est venu rendre visite à l’homme riche. L’homme riche n’a pas voulu tuer un de ses moutons ou un de ses bœufs pour faire un repas à son invité. Alors il a pris l’agnelle de l’homme pauvre et il l’a fait cuire pour le visiteur. »

sw.L: Kisha msafiri akaja kwa yule tajiri, naye akaona uchungu kutwaa katika kundi lake mwenyewe na katika ng'ombe zake mwenyewe ili kumwandalia mpita njia aliyekuja kwake. Akamtwaa mwana-kondoo wa yule maskini akamwandalia mtu aliyekuja kwake."
sw.B: Kisha mgeni alifika kwa yule tajiri. Hakutaka kuchukua mmoja wa kondoo au ng'ombe wake mwenyewe ili kumwandalia mgeni aliyekuja kwake. Basi akamchukua mwana-kondoo wa yule maskini akamwandalia mgeni wake."
sw.R: Siku moja msafiri alikuja kumtembelea yule tajiri. Tajiri hakutaka kumchinja hata mmoja wa kondoo au ng'ombe wake ili kumpikia mgeni wake chakula. Basi akamchukua mwana-kondoo wa yule maskini akampikia mgeni huyo."

vi.L: Có một khách lữ hành đến nhà người giàu, nhưng ông tiếc không lấy chiên hay bò của mình để làm thịt đãi người khách đã đến với mình. Ông bắt con chiên cái của người nghèo và làm thịt nó đãi người khách đã đến với mình."
vi.B: Một hôm có một người khách đi đường ghé nhà người giàu. Ông ta không muốn bắt chiên hay bò của mình làm thịt đãi khách, nên bắt con chiên cái của người nghèo mà làm thịt đãi khách."
vi.R: Một hôm có một người khách đến thăm người giàu. Người giàu không muốn làm thịt chiên hay bò của mình để đãi khách. Vì vậy ông ta bắt con chiên của người nghèo và nấu cho khách ăn."

ko.L: 그런데 나그네 하나가 그 부자에게 왔습니다. 그러나 그는 자기에게 온 길손을 위하여 [음식을] 장만하려고 자기 양 떼와 소 떼에서 가져오기를 아까워했습니다. 그리고 그가 가난한 사람의 암양 새끼를 빼앗아 자기에게 온 사람을 위하여 장만했습니다."
ko.B: 그런데 그 부자에게 나그네가 찾아왔습니다. 부자는 찾아온 손님을 대접하려고 자기 양이나 소를 잡기는 아까웠습니다. 그래서 그는 가난한 사람의 암양 새끼를 빼앗아다가 손님을 위해 요리했습니다."
ko.R: 어느 날 길을 가던 사람이 그 부자를 찾아왔습니다. 부자는 손님에게 대접할 음식을 만들려고 자기 양이나 소를 잡고 싶지 않았습니다. 그래서 그는 가난한 사람의 양을 빼앗아 손님을 위해 요리했습니다."

pt.L: E veio um viajante ao homem rico, e ele teve pena de tomar das suas ovelhas e dos seus bois para preparar [comida] para o viajante que tinha vindo a ele; e tomou a cordeirinha do homem pobre e a preparou para o homem que tinha vindo a ele."
pt.B: Então chegou um viajante à casa do rico. Ele teve pena de tirar uma das suas próprias ovelhas ou um dos seus bois para preparar uma refeição para o visitante que tinha chegado. Por isso tomou a cordeirinha do pobre e a preparou para o seu hóspede."
pt.R: Um dia, um viajante foi visitar o homem rico. O rico não quis matar nenhuma das suas ovelhas nem dos seus bois para fazer uma refeição para o hóspede. Então pegou a cordeirinha do pobre e a cozinhou para o visitante."

am.L: ወደ ባለ ጠጋውም ሰው እንግዳ መጣ፤ እርሱም ወደ እርሱ ለመጣው መንገደኛ ለማዘጋጀት ከበጎቹና ከከብቶቹ መውሰድ ሳሳ፤ የድሀውንም ሰው ጠቦት ወስዶ ወደ እርሱ ለመጣው ሰው አዘጋጃት።»
am.B: ከዚያም አንድ መንገደኛ ወደ ሀብታሙ ሰው መጣ። እርሱ ግን ለመጣው እንግዳ ምግብ ለማዘጋጀት ከገዛ በጎቹ ወይም ከከብቶቹ አንዱን ሊወስድ አልፈለገም። ስለዚህ የድሀውን ሰው ጠቦት ወስዶ ለእንግዳው አዘጋጃት።»
am.R: አንድ ቀን አንድ መንገደኛ ሀብታሙን ሰው ሊጠይቅ መጣ። ሀብታሙ ሰው ግን ለእንግዳው ምግብ ለማዘጋጀት ከገዛ በጎቹ ወይም ከከብቶቹ አንዱን ሊያርድ አልፈለገም። ስለዚህ የድሀውን ሰው ጠቦት ወስዶ ለእንግዳው አብስሎ አቀረባት።»

hi.L: और धनी पुरुष के पास एक बटोही आया, और उसने उस यात्री के लिए, जो उसके पास आया था, भोजन तैयार करने को अपनी भेड़-बकरियों और अपने गाय-बैलों में से लेने से हाथ खींचा; और उसने उस कंगाल पुरुष की भेड़ की बच्ची ले ली और उसे उस पुरुष के लिए तैयार किया जो उसके पास आया था।"
hi.B: तब धनी पुरुष के यहाँ एक यात्री आया। वह उस अतिथि के लिए, जो उसके पास आया था, भोजन तैयार करने को अपनी भेड़-बकरियों या गाय-बैलों में से कुछ नहीं लेना चाहता था। इसलिए उसने उस कंगाल पुरुष की भेड़ की बच्ची ले ली और उसे अपने अतिथि के लिए तैयार किया।"
hi.R: एक दिन एक यात्री उस अमीर आदमी से मिलने आया। अमीर आदमी अपने मेहमान के लिए खाना बनाने को अपनी भेड़ों या गाय-बैलों में से किसी को मारना नहीं चाहता था। इसलिए उसने उस ग़रीब आदमी की मेमनी ले ली और उसे अपने मेहमान के लिए पकाया।"

ru.L: И пришёл путник к богатому человеку, и тот пожалел взять из своего мелкого и из своего крупного скота, чтобы приготовить для странника, который пришёл к нему; и взял он овечку бедного человека и приготовил её для человека, который пришёл к нему.»
ru.B: Однажды к богатому пришёл путник. Богач пожалел взять овцу или корову из своего стада, чтобы приготовить угощение для гостя, который пришёл к нему. Он взял овечку бедняка и приготовил её для своего гостя.»
ru.R: Однажды к богатому пришёл в гости путник. Богач не захотел резать своих овец или коров, чтобы накормить гостя. Он взял овечку бедняка и приготовил из неё обед для гостя.»

ja.L: さて、富んでいる男のところに旅人が来ました。彼は、自分のところに来た旅人のために料理するのに、自分の羊や牛から取るのを惜しみ、貧しい男の雌の小羊を取って、自分のところに来た人のために料理したのです。」
ja.B: あるとき、金持ちのところに旅人がやって来ました。金持ちは、訪ねて来た客をもてなすのに、自分の羊や牛を使うのを惜しみ、貧しい人の雌の小羊を取り上げて、客のために料理したのです。」
ja.R: ある日、旅人がお金持ちのところに訪ねて来ました。お金持ちは、客のために食事を作るのに、自分の羊や牛を殺すのが惜しくなりました。それで、貧しい人の小羊を取り上げて、客のために料理したのです。」

uk.L: І прийшов подорожній до багатого чоловіка, і той пошкодував узяти зі своєї дрібної худоби й зі своєї великої худоби, щоб приготувати для мандрівника, що прийшов до нього. І взяв він овечку бідного чоловіка, і приготував її для чоловіка, що прийшов до нього.»
uk.B: Одного разу до багатого чоловіка прийшов подорожній. Той не захотів узяти когось зі своїх овець чи волів, щоб приготувати для гостя, що прийшов до нього. Тож він узяв овечку бідного чоловіка й приготував її для свого гостя.»
uk.R: Якось до багатого чоловіка прийшов подорожній. Багач не захотів різати жодної зі своїх овець чи волів, щоб приготувати їжу для гостя. Тож він забрав овечку бідного чоловіка й зварив її для гостя.»

decisions.choice: he spared: he was unwilling to part with his own animals
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel pity for something and so hold it back. The rich man "spares" his own animals, yet in verse 6 David condemns him because he "had no pity": the same verb, turned against him.

decisions.choice: a traveler: a guest who had to be fed
decisions.reason: Hospitality was a strict duty, and a guest was given a meal of meat (Genesis 18:1-8). The visitor is named three ways, "a traveler", "the wayfarer" and "the man who had come to him", but he is the same person.

decisions.choice: prepare: kill and cook for a meal
decisions.reason: "To make" or "prepare" an animal for a guest means to slaughter it and cook it (Genesis 18:7-8).

decisions.choice: did not want to (Balanced); visitor, guest (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "did not want to" for "spared", and use "visitor" and "guest" for the three names of the traveler so that it is clear one man is meant.

decisions.choice: One day; kill; make a meal; cooked
decisions.reason: Readable sets the scene with "One day" and spells out what preparing an animal for a guest involved (m3).

decisions.choice: "tiếc" (L); "không muốn" (B, R)
decisions.reason: He was unwilling to part with his own animals (meaning decision); Literal's "tiếc" (begrudge) keeps the link with "had no pity" in verse 6.

decisions.choice: teve pena de tomar (L); teve pena de tirar (B)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "ter pena" covers both sides of the verb: to be sorry to part with something and to feel pity for someone (m1). Literal and Balanced use it here so that David's verdict in verse 6, "não teve pena", turns the same words against the rich man (m4 there). Readable says "não quis", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "हाथ खींचा" for "spared" (Literal)
decisions.reason: He was unwilling to part with his own animals (m1). The same Hebrew verb returns in verse 6, "he had no pity"; Hindi cannot keep one verb for both, so Literal uses "हाथ खींचना" here and "तरस" there.

decisions.choice: "пожалел" (Literal, Balanced); "не захотел" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 6, "не пожалел" (meaning m4 there); Literal and Balanced keep "жалеть" in both verses so that the rich man's sparing his own flock answers his not sparing the poor man.

decisions.choice: chamal "惜しむ" at every level
decisions.reason: The same verb as "had no pity" in 12:6 (12:6 m4); Japanese uses 惜しむ here and あわれまなかった there, as the English uses two words.

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף דָּוִ֛ד בָּאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֑ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־נָתָ֔ן חַי־יְהוָ֕ה כִּ֣י בֶן־מָ֔וֶת הָאִ֖ישׁ הָעֹשֶׂ֥ה זֹֽאת׃

records.literal_gloss: And burned [the] anger of David against the man very, and he said to Nathan, [as] lives Yahweh, surely a son of death [is] the man who did this.

en.L: And David's anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives, the man who did this [is] a son of death!
en.B: David's anger burned hot against the man. "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," he said to Nathan, "the man who did this deserves to die!
en.R: David became very angry with the rich man. "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives," he told Nathan, "the man who did this should die!

es.L: Y se encendió mucho la ira de David contra aquel hombre, y dijo a Natán: «¡Vive {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que hijo de muerte [es] el hombre que hizo esto!
es.B: La ira de David se encendió mucho contra aquel hombre. «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive», le dijo a Natán, «¡el hombre que hizo esto merece la muerte!
es.R: David se enojó muchísimo con el hombre rico. «Tan cierto como que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive», le dijo a Natán, «¡el hombre que hizo esto debe morir!

fr.L: Et la colère de David s’enflamma très fort contre l’homme, et il dit à Nathan : « [Aussi vrai que] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, l’homme qui a fait cela [est] un fils de la mort !
fr.B: David s’enflamma de colère contre cet homme. « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, dit-il à Nathan, l’homme qui a fait cela mérite la mort !
fr.R: David s’est mis très en colère contre l’homme riche. « Aussi vrai que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est vivant, a-t-il dit à Nathan, l’homme qui a fait cela devrait mourir !

sw.L: Hasira ya Daudi ikawaka sana juu ya mtu huyo, akamwambia Nathani, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, mtu aliyefanya hivi [ni] mwana wa mauti!
sw.B: Hasira ya Daudi iliwaka sana dhidi ya mtu huyo. Akamwambia Nathani, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, mtu aliyefanya jambo hili anastahili kufa!
sw.R: Daudi alimkasirikia sana yule tajiri. Akamwambia Nathani, "Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aishivyo, mtu aliyefanya jambo hili anapaswa kufa!

vi.L: Đa-vít nổi giận phừng phừng với người ấy, và nói với Na-than: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, người đã làm điều này đáng chết!
vi.B: Đa-vít nổi giận phừng phừng với người ấy và nói với Na-than: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, kẻ đã làm điều này đáng phải chết!
vi.R: Đa-vít rất giận người giàu ấy. Vua nói với Na-than: "Thật như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} hằng sống, kẻ đã làm điều này phải chết!

ko.L: 그러자 다윗이 그 사람에게 몹시 분노하여 나단에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 [두고 맹세하는데], 이 일을 한 사람은 죽어 마땅한 자[이다]!
ko.B: 다윗은 그 사람에게 크게 분노하여 나단에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세하는데, 그런 일을 한 사람은 죽어 마땅하다!
ko.R: 다윗은 그 부자에게 몹시 화가 났다. 그가 나단에게 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 살아 계심을 두고 맹세한다. 그런 짓을 한 사람은 죽어야 한다!

pt.L: E a ira de Davi se acendeu muito contra o homem, e ele disse a Natã: "[Tão certo como] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive, o homem que fez isso [é] filho da morte!
pt.B: A ira de Davi se acendeu muito contra aquele homem. "Tão certo como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive", disse ele a Natã, "o homem que fez isso merece morrer!
pt.R: Davi ficou furioso com o homem rico. "Tão certo como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} vive", disse ele a Natã, "o homem que fez isso deve morrer!

am.L: የዳዊትም ቁጣ በሰውየው ላይ እጅግ ነደደ፤ ናታንንም አለው፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕያው ነውና፣ ይህን ያደረገ ሰው የሞት ልጅ [ነው]!
am.B: የዳዊት ቁጣ በሰውየው ላይ እጅግ ነደደ። ናታንንም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕያው ነውና» አለው፤ «ይህን ያደረገ ሰው ሞት ይገባዋል!
am.R: ዳዊት በሀብታሙ ሰው ላይ እጅግ ተቆጣ። ናታንንም፦ «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕያው እንደ ሆነ በእርግጥ» አለው፤ «ይህን ያደረገ ሰው መሞት አለበት!

hi.L: तब दाऊद का क्रोध उस पुरुष पर बहुत भड़का, और उसने नातान से कहा, "जीवित {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की शपथ, जिस पुरुष ने यह किया है वह मृत्यु के योग्य [है]!
hi.B: दाऊद का क्रोध उस पुरुष पर बहुत भड़क उठा। "जीवित {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की शपथ," उसने नातान से कहा, "जिस पुरुष ने यह किया है, वह मृत्यु के योग्य है!
hi.R: दाऊद को उस अमीर आदमी पर बहुत क्रोध आया। "जीवित {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की शपथ," उसने नातान से कहा, "जिस आदमी ने यह किया है, उसे मार डाला जाना चाहिए!

ru.L: И сильно разгорелся гнев Давида на того человека, и он сказал Нафану: «[Как] жив {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}, сын смерти тот человек, который сделал это!
ru.B: Давид страшно разгневался на того человека. «Как верно то, что жив {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}», — сказал он Нафану, — «человек, который сделал это, заслуживает смерти!
ru.R: Давид очень разозлился на богача. «Как верно то, что жив {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}}», — сказал он Нафану, — «человек, который сделал это, должен умереть!

ja.L: ダビデはその男に対して激しく怒りを燃やし、ナタンに言った。「{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は生きておられる。このことをした男は死の子だ。
ja.B: ダビデはその男に対して激しく怒った。「{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は生きておられる」と彼はナタンに言った。「そんなことをした男は死に値する。
ja.R: ダビデは、そのお金持ちに対してひどく怒りました。「生きておられる{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}にかけて誓う」とダビデはナタンに言いました。「そんなことをした男は死ななければならない。

uk.L: І дуже запалав гнів Давида на того чоловіка, і сказав він Натанові: «[Як] живий {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, син смерті той чоловік, що зробив це!
uk.B: Давидів гнів сильно запалав на того чоловіка. «Як живий {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}», — сказав він Натанові, — «чоловік, що зробив це, заслуговує на смерть!
uk.R: Давид дуже розгнівався на того багача. «Як живий {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}», — сказав він Натанові, — «чоловік, що зробив це, повинен померти!

decisions.choice: as the LORD lives: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: David swears by the life of Yahweh, which binds him to his own verdict (1 Samuel 14:39; 20:3). Without knowing it, he passes sentence on himself under oath.

decisions.choice: a son of death: a man who deserves to die
decisions.reason: "Son of" with a quality means a person marked by it. "Son of death" is someone who deserves death or is doomed to it (1 Samuel 20:31; 26:16).

decisions.choice: a verdict beyond the law
decisions.reason: The law for stealing a sheep was repayment, not death (Exodus 21:37, numbered 22:1 in some Bibles), as David himself goes on to say in verse 6. His outburst shows how wicked the rich man's act seems to him. Some take "son of death" as a cry of contempt ("he deserves to die") rather than a legal sentence.

decisions.choice: deserves to die (Balanced); should die (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m2); Literal keeps "son of death".

decisions.choice: "đáng chết" (L)
decisions.reason: A man who deserves to die (meaning decision); Vietnamese "con của sự chết" would not be understood, so Literal gives the sense in the shortest form.

decisions.choice: "죽어 마땅한 자" at Literal for "a son of death"
decisions.reason: A word-for-word "son of death" would mislead a Korean reader; Literal gives the idiom's sense in a short phrase, as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: filho da morte (L); merece morrer (B); deve morrer (R)
decisions.reason: As 1 Samuel 20:31 and 26:16 in Portuguese: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, and Balanced and Readable give its meaning (m2). The oath takes the book's form "tão certo como o SENHOR vive" (m1).

decisions.choice: "As the LORD lives" is «{{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ሕያው ነውና» at Literal and Balanced; Readable «… ሕያው እንደ ሆነ በእርግጥ», as the English Readable
decisions.reason: The oath formula of the terms list for Joshua to 2 Samuel, so that it reads alike wherever it recurs.

decisions.choice: "जीवित {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की शपथ"; "मृत्यु के योग्य" (Literal, Balanced), "उसे मार डाला जाना चाहिए" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The oath as 1 Samuel 14:39 and 25:26; "son of death" as 1 Samuel 26:16 ("मृत्यु के योग्य"), the Hebrew idiom for one who deserves to die (m2).

decisions.choice: "[Как] жив ГОСПОДЬ" (Literal); "Как верно то, что жив ГОСПОДЬ" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The oath keeps the wording 1 Samuel settles at each level.

decisions.choice: "сын смерти" (Literal); "заслуживает смерти" (Balanced); "должен умереть" (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom, as 1 Samuel 26:16 does; the other levels give its sense (meaning m2).

decisions.choice: one quotation broken by "— сказал он Нафану, —"
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable break David's speech with "he said to Nathan" and count two quotations; Russian keeps two pairs of marks, as the style guide settles for a speech broken by a verb of saying.

decisions.choice: chai YHWH "{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}は生きておられる" (L, B), "生きておられる{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}にかけて誓う" (R)
decisions.reason: As 1 SA 20:3.

decisions.choice: ben mavet "死の子" (L), "死に値する" (B), "死ななければならない" (R)
decisions.reason: A man who deserves to die (m2).

decisions.choice: repay fourfold: the penalty the law set for a stolen sheep
decisions.reason: Exodus 21:37 (numbered 22:1 in some Bibles) says that whoever steals a sheep and slaughters it must repay four sheep for it. David the judge applies the law exactly.

decisions.choice: fourfold, as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation read "sevenfold", a number used for full repayment in Proverbs 6:31. The Hebrew reading agrees with the law of Exodus 21:37 and is followed.

decisions.choice: fourfold: a number that may look ahead in David's story
decisions.reason: Readers have long noticed that four of David's sons die in what follows: the child (verse 18), Amnon (13:28-29), Absalom (18:14-15) and Adonijah (1 Kings 2:25). The text does not draw this link itself.

decisions.choice: he had no pity: the same verb as "spared" in verse 4
decisions.reason: The rich man was sparing with his own flock but had no pity on the poor man. The wordplay sharpens the charge.

decisions.choice: pay the poor man back four lambs for the one he took
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "fourfold" means here.

decisions.choice: "चौगुना" (Literal, Balanced); "एक के बदले चार" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The penalty of the law for a stolen sheep (m1), as the Hebrew text reads (m2).

decisions.choice: "вчетверо" (Literal, Balanced); "четырёх овец за ту одну" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The penalty the law set for a stolen sheep (meaning m1, Exodus 22:1).
